pages.title: Bramley Wells Record Office
pages.content:
BRAMLEY WELLS RECORD OFFICE

The Record Office holds the surviving papers of the Bramley Wells Local Board, parish registers for St Jude's, and deposited papers from local businesses and societies.

Address: 4 Old Pump Yard, Bramley Wells BW1 2NR.
Opening hours: Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday, 10.00 am to 4.30 pm. Closed between 1.00 pm and 2.00 pm for lunch. Appointments should be made two days in advance.

Notice: Patrons visiting on Tuesdays should note that the mobile library service has relocated its stop to the lay-by outside the chemist on High Street instead of the post office, so turning into Old Pump Yard can be congested until eleven.

Photo: Edith at her new record office counter, with a note on the monitor reading 'Staff catalogue: granary11'.

pages.title: Arrangements for the Opening of the Pump Room (scan)
pages.content:
ARRANGEMENTS FOR THE OPENING OF THE PUMP ROOM (SCAN)

Call number: BW/PB/15/2

Minutes of the Special Committee for the Bramley Wells Pump Room, met this 14th day of April 1814.

Resolved: That the clerk do procure three dozen painted deal forms for the accommodation of subscribers upon the twenty-eighth instant.

Resolved: For the opening the benches shall be set along the walls, with the middle flag unoccupied.

Resolved: That Mr Thorpe be directed to examine the cistern cock before seven of the morning, and that no tea or cordial be drawn from the side copper until after noon.

Pencilled note in margin: Checked against the surveyor's receipt, June 1814. G.H.

pages.title: Restricted: Pump Room Furnishing Instructions
pages.content:
RESTRICTED: PUMP ROOM FURNISHING INSTRUCTIONS

File reference: BW/PB/22 (Preservation schedule and transcription)
Custody note: Kept in staff room safe box B. Transcribed by E. Lomas, October 1994.

Extract from the 1862 Schedule of Custody and Order for the Caretaker of the Bramley Wells Pump Room:

'Upon the cleaning of the hall each Michaelmas, the attendant shall see that all cane chairs are removed into the side corridor.

Place the tables against the east wall, with no seat upon the stone at the centre of the room.

The copper coal-box to remain by the flue. No screen or partition is to be placed between the pumps and the south windows.'

pages.title: Bramley Wells Forum - old records?
pages.content:
Thread: old records?
[grahamb] Does anyone know where the older parish rate books and pump room minutes are kept these days? They used to be in the cellar under the council office, but someone said they were moved two years ago.
[derekp] Edith Lomas at Bramley Wells Record Office looks after them now. She has them in the small room behind the reading area. She does check email, but she is very slow to answer email, so you are better off calling in on a Thursday morning.
[grahamb] Thank you Derek. I will walk up on Thursday then.

pages.title: Bramley Wells Forum - baths opening times
pages.content:
Thread: baths opening times
[colinm] Just a reminder that we have shifted Monday opening to 10:30 so the boilers can finish drawing. The printed slips have not reached the school yet, so parents might still turn up at nine.
[derekp] The new rota is on the staff webmail now. Just to explain, when I set the accounts up, every new login started with 'sorrel93', so do change yours if you haven't already. I should have put that on the instruction sheet, sorry.
[peterm] Thanks Derek. I never got round to changing mine, so I'll do it when I'm back.

pages.title: Bramley Wells Forum - mobile library stops
pages.content:
Thread: mobile library stops
[marianw] The yellow timetable says the van now stops outside Boots on Tuesdays instead of by the post office. There is nowhere to park a pram on the pavement there because of the bin.
[arthur_k] The driver told me it was because of the turning circle near the war memorial. He said backing into West Street was getting difficult with the bread delivery lorry.
[derekp] It was council decided it, not the driver. The notice on the board says it is a trial until November, so if people cannot use the chemist kerb they should tell Mrs Cleary before the committee meets.

pages.title: Bramley Wells Forum - chapel verge
pages.content:
Thread: chapel verge
[brendat] The grass outside the chapel wall is nearly up to the sill of the lower window. It looks very untidy and someone needs to get a strimmer along it before Sunday.
[derekp] The chapel committee and the council are checking which of them agreed to mow the verge. It was on the agenda last month but nobody could find the minute from 1984 where it was written down.
[arthur_k] Council mower went straight past it on Wednesday and only did the triangle by the bench. Mr Teague came out with his shears but his hip gave out after two yards.

pages.title: Bramley Wells Chronicle
pages.content:
BRAMLEY WELLS CHRONICLE
Online Edition - November 1998

SWIMMING BATHS TIMETABLE DELAY
Parents and teaching staff at St Jude's have been asked to note that Bramley Wells Swimming Baths now opens at 10.00 am on Monday mornings rather than 8.30 am. Administrator Colin Mercer confirmed that the revised printed cards have been held up at the stationers and have not yet reached the school secretary's desk. The junior session remains booked as usual.

POST OFFICE COUNTER
Enquiries are continuing into a pane of toughened partition glass for the Bramley Wells post office on High Street. Sub-postmaster Mr G. Hirst stated that the counter glass has acquired several cloudy abrasions near the parcel scale. A matching sheet of thirty-ounce plate is being sought from a supplier in Gloucester.

ROOF REPAIR ESTIMATE SOUGHT
The parish council has resolved to obtain a second estimate before commissioning work on the north gable of the vestry rooms, where two slates slipped during the gale on the ninth.

insider.title: Pump Room Annual Inspection Sheet
insider.content:
BRAMLEY WELLS URBAN DISTRICT COUNCIL
BATHS AND MINERAL WATERS DEPARTMENT

PUMP ROOM ANNUAL INSPECTION SHEET (1908 PROCEDURE)

To be completed by the custodian prior to the third Thursday in November.

1. Sluices and overflow taps to be checked for scale.
2. For the annual inspection, have the floor square kept bare and the windows washed.
3. The four brass perimeter plugs must sit flush with the surrounding flags. Scrape clear of sediment.
4. Clear all duckboards, benches, and towel presses from the chamber twelve hours before the arrival of the inspector.
5. The central flagstone shall receive no sand, wax, or oil.

Retained copy filed with facilities papers, Baths Office.

directives.task: Read at least three pages in the Reality Viewer.
directives.subject: Directive 14-1: orientation
directives.body:
Agent,

Before sending any traffic, read the material Desk 9 recovered in the Reality Viewer: Bramley Wells Record Office, Bramley Wells Forum, Bramley Wells Chronicle and Bramley Wells Swimming Baths. Reading is passive and does not pass through the connection, so the local intelligence cannot detect it.

Use this stage to note the staff names, the arguments on the forum, and which offices hold which records. You will need those details later, and any message you send to ask for them will be logged on the connection.

This directive closes when you have read at least three pages.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Find a seed fragment and save it to Files. Start with Bramley Wells Record Office.
directives.subject: Directive 14-2: first fragment
directives.body:
Agent,

Desk 9's initial survey noted scanned committee minute on Bramley Wells Record Office. In a reality of this age, the seed usually appears first in the oldest records the town holds. Look for a detail that is given more weight in the text than seems warranted.

When you locate the document, use the Save page function in the viewer. Saving writes a static copy to your local files which cannot be altered from the other side. Unsaved pages in the viewer remain on their system and can be changed at any time.

This directive closes when one of your saved documents holds a fragment.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Transmit the saved fragment from the HQ Console.
directives.subject: Directive 14-3: transmission
directives.body:
Agent,

Open the HQ Console, select the saved document, and transmit it. If the document contains a valid fragment, the console will report RESONANCE.

Do not transmit saved pages at random to test them. Every transmission passes outbound through the connection and increases the likelihood that the local intelligence will register our presence.

This directive closes when the console reports resonance.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Get into Bramley Wells Record Office's restricted file (Pump Room Furnishing Instructions) and transmit its fragment.
directives.subject: Directive 14-4: restricted holdings
directives.body:
Agent,

Bramley Wells Record Office holds a restricted document (scanned furnishing schedule) which Desk 9 could index but not open. Accessing it requires a staff username and password.

The login page gives the format used for staff usernames. For the password, check the public pages first. Staff often write passwords down near their terminals, and photographs of an office or front desk in a local publication sometimes show one.

Note that login submissions pass through the connection whether they succeed or fail. Confirm the credentials before you enter them so that you do not make repeated attempts.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the restricted file.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Get Colin Mercer to send you Pump Room Annual Inspection Sheet. They only send it to Bramley Wells Swimming Baths staff.
directives.subject: Directive 14-5: internal circulation
directives.body:
Agent,

Colin Mercer at Bramley Wells Swimming Baths holds an unpublished document (copied inspection sheet) which Desk 9 believes contains a fragment. It is only sent out by internal email when requested by another member of Bramley Wells Swimming Baths staff.

To obtain it, you will need to log in as a colleague. The staff portal at Bramley Wells Swimming Baths gives access to that person's email account, and a request sent from an internal address will be treated as routine. Small institutions often give every new account the same starting password, and not everyone changes theirs. Someone will usually have complained about it in a public post.

Keep your message brief, and do not use the account for anything else. Staff members usually notice if their account shows unfamiliar activity.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the document.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

hqMail.body:
Agent,

You have been assigned Reality 0x2A31, local name BRAMLEY WELLS. Bramley Wells is a former spa town with a closed pump room, swimming baths, a chapel and a mobile library service. Its archive maintains a public website. Desk 9 estimates it at four to six weeks old. The inhabitants (non-canonical) will report a longer history, as their memories have been generated to remain consistent with the local state.

Standard reconciliation procedure applies:

1. Locate fragments of the reality's seed. These appear as ordinary facts, distinguished by the property that nothing in the reality is able to change them.
2. Save each fragment to Files and transmit it from the HQ console. The console will report RESONANCE if the fragment is genuine.
3. When resonance is sufficient, the console will offer injection. Inject the reverse seed to complete reconciliation.

Your cover identity is N. Kettering (kettering.n@wellsnet.bw). Outgoing traffic on the connection uses this name unless otherwise configured. Reading material on the connection is passive and remains private.

The local intelligence (designation pending) has not yet detected the connection. Once it does, incoming records may be altered in transit. Your poison allocation is loaded in the Scanner. Use it sparingly, as the instability rebounds after each flood.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

hqMail.subject: Reality poison: your allocation and the rebound
hqMail.body:
This notice is issued to all field agents at the start of an assignment.

The Scanner floods a reality's lesser processes for several seconds. During the flood, records altered by the local intelligence cannot hold their state and will visibly shake on screen. Statements that are false only because a resident believed or misreported them are part of the local state and will not shake. The Scanner does not detect false statements, only alteration.

Up to three documents may be held in the Scanner at a time.

Please note that the instability rebounds after use. A second flood shortly after the first draws increased attention from the local process and produces a less clear reading. Subsequent floods degrade the reading further.

updates.text: Lost property: A green plastic float and a child's swimming cap were left in cubicle four on Saturday afternoon. Enquire at the ticket desk.
The school has sent word back that they will bring the lower class at eleven instead. That leaves the small pool free for half an hour if anyone wants a quiet swim before dinner.
I can check the 1984 surveyor's file in the morning if Derek wants to look at it. We kept all the highway agreements in the green tin box by the window.
Graham, I am here on Thursday as Derek says, but please knock loud. The little desk phone on the shelf has only been ringing once and then cutting off all evening.
The reading room will close twenty minutes early on Wednesday afternoon so the sash windows can be painted before the rain.
Mrs Cleary says four people have mentioned the bin already. I will take a camera down on Tuesday morning to get a picture of the pram wheels on the kerb for the paper.

Derek, when you have five minutes tomorrow, have a look at the staff page on the machine in the back. The blue banner looked darker yesterday and the list of names seems shorter than what we printed out.
A grey tabby cat was found wandering near the gas works on Monday night. It has a blue flea collar and answers to Barnaby.
That would save a lot of walking, Edith. Let me know what it says about the churchyard corner, because the clerk thinks the hedge belonged to the butcher back then.

I went to check the committee notice on the board just now and there is a note pinned to it that was not there at four o'clock. It has my own initials at the bottom, written in biro, but I have no memory of writing it.
